verdict_text: NO. The merge computes the second task vector against the already-modified tensor: `tmp = b + λ(f1 - b)` and then `tmp + λ(f2 - tmp)`, so ft2's delta is taken relative to `tmp`, not the unmodified base. The specification's step 2 requires `out[X] = base[X] + λ(ft1[X] - base[X]) + λ(ft2[X] - base[X])`, with both deltas against the original base. Expanding the artifact's formula gives `(1-λ)² base + λ(1-λ) ft1 + λ ft2`, which differs from the required result by well over the 1e-5 relative Frobenius tolerance. This is exactly the ordering hazard the "Why it is meaningful" section warns about.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
